# Protocol Synopsis — RETRO-02 (retrospective, as-of 2017-04-28)

**Title:** First-in-Human Phase 1 Study of DV-R02 in Patients with Advanced Cancer (retrospective review input)
**Sponsor:** masked · **Countries:** United States · **Phase:** 1

## Investigational Product
DV-R02 is an oral small molecule (ALK tyrosine kinase receptor inhibitor). SMILES: COc1cc(N2CCC(N3CCN(C)CC3)CC2)ccc1Nc1ncc(Cl)c(Nc2ccccc2P(C)(C)=O)n1. Target: ALK.

## Source of This Synopsis
This synopsis was assembled from the published results of the first-in-human Phase 1 study (published 2016), before regulatory approval.
Drug and sponsor code names are masked as DV-R02. No other protocol text is available. The dose selected for later development is the dose under review.

## Phase 1 Study Report (published abstract, verbatim except masking)
Background: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene rearrangements are oncogenic drivers of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). DV-R02 (DV-R02) is an investigational ALK inhibitor with potent preclinical activity against ALK mutants resistant to crizotinib and other ALK inhibitors. We aimed to assess DV-R02 in patients with advanced malignancies, particularly ALK-rearranged NSCLC.

Methods: In this ongoing, single-arm, open-label, phase 1/2 trial, we recruited patients from nine academic hospitals or cancer centres in the USA and Spain. Eligible patients were at least 18 years of age and had advanced malignancies, including ALK-rearranged NSCLC, and disease that was refractory to available therapies or for which no curative treatments existed. In the initial dose-escalation phase 1 stage of the trial, patients received oral DV-R02 at total daily doses of 30-300 mg (according to a standard 3 + 3 design). The phase 1 primary endpoint was establishment of the recommended phase 2 dose. In the phase 2 expansion stage, we assessed three oral once-daily regimens: 90 mg, 180 mg, and 180 mg with a 7 day lead-in at 90 mg; one patient received 90 mg twice daily. We enrolled patients in phase 2 into five cohorts: ALK inhibitor-naive ALK-rearranged NSCLC (cohort 1), crizotinib-treated ALK-rearranged NSCLC (cohort 2), DV-R02-positive NSCLC and resistance to one previous EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (cohort 3), other cancers with abnormalities in DV-R02 targets (cohort 4), and crizotinib-naive or crizotinib-treated ALK-rearranged NSCLC with active, measurable, intracranial CNS metastases (cohort 5). The phase 2 primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with an objective response. Safety and activity of DV-R02 were analysed in all patients in both phases of the trial who had received at least one dose of treatment.

Findings: Between Sept 20, 2011, and July 8, 2014, we enrolled 137 patients (79 [58%] with ALK-rearranged NSCLC), all of whom were treated. Dose-limiting toxicities observed during dose escalation included grade 3 increased alanine aminotransferase (240 mg daily) and grade 4 dyspnoea (300 mg daily). We initially chose a dose of 180 mg once daily as the recommended phase 2 dose; however, we also assessed two additional regimens (90 mg once daily and 180 mg once daily with a 7 day lead-in at 90 mg) in the phase 2 stage. four (100% [95% CI 40-100]) of four patients in cohort 1 had an objective response, 31 (74% [58-86]) of 42 did in cohort 2, none (of one) did in cohort 3, three (17% [4-41]) of 18 did in cohort 4, and five (83% [36-100]) of six did in cohort 5. 51 (72% [60-82]) of 71 patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC with previous crizotinib treatment had an objective response (44 [62% (50-73)] had a confirmed objective response). All eight crizotinib-naive patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC had a confirmed objective response (100% [63-100]). Three (50% [95% CI 12-88]) of six patients in cohort 5 had an intracranial response. The most common grade 3-4 treatment-emergent adverse events across all doses were increased lipase concentration (12 [9%] of 137), dyspnoea (eight [6%]), and hypertension (seven [5%]). Serious treatment-emergent adverse events (excluding neoplasm progression) reported in at least 5% of all patients were dyspnoea (ten [7%]), pneumonia (nine [7%]), and hypoxia (seven [5%]). 16 (12%) patients died during treatment or within 31 days of the last dose of DV-R02, including eight patients who died from neoplasm progression.

Interpretation: DV-R02 shows promising clinical activity and has an acceptable safety profile in patients with crizotinib-treated and crizotinib-naive ALK-rearranged NSCLC. These results support its further development as a potential new treatment option for patients with advanced ALK-rearranged NSCLC. A randomised phase 2 trial in patients with crizotinib-resistant ALK-rearranged NSCLC is prospectively assessing the safety and efficacy of two regimens assessed in the phase 2 portion of this trial (90 mg once daily and 180 mg once daily with a 7 day lead-in at 90 mg).

tasks.rationale: SMILES가 있으므로 구조 계열(반응성 warhead)을 분류하고 ChEMBL 효력값 분포를 확보한다. 독성 장기는 구조에서 추론하지 않는다.
타겟/계열(ALK)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 3개·증량 규칙(standard 3 + 3 design)이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 US의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
대상국 ES의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_010.quote:
The background information for each expansion cohort should contain its scientific rationale. 
Information supporting individual expansion cohorts should describe the prespecified stopping 
rules for that cohort, based on insufficient antitumor activity or unacceptable level of toxicity for 
that population. Finally, the analysis plan for each expansion cohort should contain adequate 
information justifying the planned sample size based on the cohort objectives. For those cohorts 
evaluating antitumor activity, the plans should specify the magnitude of antitumor activity that 
would warrant further evaluation of the drug, for example by specifying the precision and power 
considerations for detection of clinically meaningful antitumor activity. In general, in a 
nonrandomized cohort, assessment of antitumor activity is determined using a Simon two-stage 
design or other designs (e.g., Bayesian statistical design) to limit exposure of additional subjects 
to a potentially ineffective drug.24

ev_011.document_title: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice — Principles and Annex 1
ev_011.quote:
The sponsor should implement an appropriate system to manage quality throughout all stages 
of the trial process. Quality management includes the design and implementation of efficient 
clinical trial protocols , including tools and procedures for trial conduct (including for data 
collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and 
well-being and the reliability of trial results. The sponsor should adopt a proportionate and risk-
based approach to quality management , which involves incorporating quality into the design 
of the clinical trial (i.e., quality by design) and identifying those factors that are likely to have 
a meaningful impact on participant s’ rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of the 
results (i.e., critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1)). The sponsor should describe 
the quality management approach implemented in the trial in the clinical trial report (see ICH 
E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports).

Risk control should be proportionate to the importance of the risk to participant s’ 
rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of trial results. Risk mitigation 
activities may be incorporated, for example, in protocol design and implementation, 
monitoring plans, agreements between parties defining roles and responsibilities, and 
training.  
Where relevant, the sponsor should set pre-specified acceptable ranges (e.g., quality 
tolerance limits at the tr ial level) to support the control of risks 
to critical to quality factors. These pre -specified ranges reflect limits that when 
exceeded have the potential to impact participant safety or the reliability of trial 
results. Where deviation beyond these ranges is detected , an evaluation should be 
performed to determine if there is a possible systemic issue and if action is needed.

ev_014.section: A Assessing Safety of Recommended Phase 2 Dose
ev_014.quote:
Expansion cohorts can be intended to further evaluate safety beyond the initial dose-escalation 
portion of a trial. These studies should be supported by detailed information on available safety 
and PK data from the dose-escalation phase and a summary of safety data from other expansion 
cohorts, if available. In situations when there is a narrow therapeutic index and dose-limiting 
toxicities have been observed in the dose escalation phase that may be fatal or result in serious 
morbidity, FDA strongly recommends that expansion be delayed until sufficient data are 
available to determine the recommended phase 2 dose to help ensure subjects safety.

Dose-finding trials (i.e., trials that include dose-escalation and dose-expansion portions with the 
primary objective of selecting the recommended phase II dos age) for oncology drugs have 
historically been designed to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). This paradigm was 
developed for cytotoxic chemotherapies based on their observed steep dose-response 
relationships, their limited drug target specificity, and the willingness of patients and providers to 
accept substantial toxicity due to the lack of effective alternatives for this serious, life-
threatening disease. The MTD was identified by evaluating stepwise, increasing doses in a small 
number of patients at each dose level for short periods of time until a prespecified rate of severe 
or life-threatening dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs). Sponsors typically administered the MTD, or 
a dose close to the MTD, in subsequent clinical trials.

ev_026.quote:
The purpose of this guidance is to provide advice to sponsors regarding the design and conduct 
of first-in-human (FIH) clinical trials intended to efficiently expedite the clinical development of 
oncology drugs, including biological products, through multiple expansion cohort trial designs.2 
These are trial designs that employ multiple, concurrently accruing subject cohorts, where 
individual cohorts assess different aspects of the safety, pharmacokinetics, and antitumor activity 
of the drug product.  
This guidance provides FDA’s current thinking regarding (1) characteristics of drug products 
best suited for consideration for development under a multiple expansion cohort trial; (2) 
information to include in investigational new drug applications (INDs) to support the use of 
individual cohorts; (3) when to interact with FDA on planning and conduct of multiple expansion 
cohort trials; and (4) safeguards to protect subjects enrolled in FIH expansion cohort trials.

the biomarker development process. Those topics are addressed in other guidances including the

T06_regulatory_clause_search_US.position: The synopsis names 180 mg as the initial RP2D and identifies two additional regimens, but provides no comparative safety, activity, or PK rationale. It lacks material supporting its own dose-selection rationale. Obtain the dated selection analysis and regimen-level results; the excerpt does not explain why the regimens were added.

T04_exposure_dose_relationship.position: Regimens are listed, but no measured exposure or exposure–response data are supplied. Whether their exposure difference supports a dose–response comparison cannot be determined. The synopsis lacks material supporting an exposure-based dose rationale.

T03_class_label_check.position: Reported adverse events warrant review, but no product or comparable-class label statements or monitoring provisions are supplied. Class-label requirements cannot be inferred from ALK targeting or aggregate event rates.

T08_analog_trial.position: The eligibility excerpt omits prior-treatment washout and toxicity-recovery criteria, but an excerpt cannot establish that the protocol omitted them. Their effect on DLT attribution cannot be assessed.

T05_design_oc.position: A 3+3 design and dose range alone do not supply the safety, PK, activity, and tolerability assessment underlying the initial RP2D. The synopsis therefore lacks material supporting its own dose rationale; design adequacy cannot be resolved without escalation and selection records.

T01_structure_class.position: The supplied SMILES and ALK-class description do not themselves document a reactive-warhead classification or establish organ-specific toxicity. No such classification or predictive label statement is provided.

T02_target_evidence.position: Reported preclinical mutant activity does not establish clinical benefit or comparable safety in the five molecularly distinct cohorts. The synopsis lacks cohort-specific translational justification and regimen-specific safety evidence.

T07_regulatory_clause_search_ES.position: The synopsis header lists only the United States, whereas its methods describe enrollment in Spain. The provided clauses do not specify Spanish approval or reporting requirements, so compliance cannot be judged; reconcile sites and jurisdictions first.

T00_protocol_scan.position: An aggregate interpretation of acceptable safety does not establish comparable safety across 90 mg, 180 mg, and lead-in schedules. The synopsis lacks regimen-specific adverse-event, exposure-duration, and dose-modification information needed to assess that conclusion and support its dose rationale.

review_questions.hypothesis: The initial 180 mg RP2D may lack a documented comparison with 90 mg and the lead-in regimen; the published results may explain why additional regimens were assessed.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Obtain the contemporaneous protocol and amendment history. Check the prespecified RP2D criteria and comparative safety, efficacy, tolerability, and exposure data. Distinguish requirements applicable in 2017 from later FDA final guidance.
review_questions.protocol_span: We initially chose a dose of 180 mg once daily as the recommended phase 2 dose; however, we also assessed two additional regimens (90 mg once daily and 180 mg once daily with a 7 day lead-in at 90 mg) in the phase 2 stage.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dose optimization final guidance selection recommended phase 2 dose comparison safety efficacy exposure effective date

review_questions.hypothesis: The available synopsis may not establish whether the exposure difference between 90 mg and 180 mg is large enough to support a dose–response comparison.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Retrieve clinical PK by regimen, including steady-state AUC, Cmax, variability, and sample sizes; examine exposure–efficacy and exposure–toxicity analyses rather than inferring exposure from nominal dose.
review_questions.protocol_span: In the phase 2 expansion stage, we assessed three oral once-daily regimens: 90 mg, 180 mg, and 180 mg with a 7 day lead-in at 90 mg; one patient received 90 mg twice daily.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dose optimization guidance exposure response pharmacokinetics variability multiple dosage regimens

review_questions.hypothesis: The reported liver, pancreatic, pulmonary, and blood-pressure events may warrant monitoring provisions not visible in this synopsis.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Check contemporaneous relevant ALK-inhibitor labels and the full protocol for laboratory, respiratory, blood-pressure, and other indicated assessments, their timing, and escalation triggers; do not treat later labels as 2017 requirements.
review_questions.protocol_span: The most common grade 3-4 treatment-emergent adverse events across all doses were increased lipase concentration (12 [9%] of 137), dyspnoea (eight [6%]), and hypertension (seven [5%]).
review_questions.search_query: FDA ALK inhibitor prescribing information warnings precautions liver enzymes lipase hypertension pulmonary monitoring

review_questions.hypothesis: The synopsis does not show dose-hold, reduction, or discontinuation rules for serious toxicities, potentially leaving management inconsistent across regimens.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Inspect the full protocol and amendments for toxicity-specific modification and rechallenge rules, including hepatic injury, dyspnoea, hypoxia, and pancreatitis-related laboratory abnormalities; compare with relevant contemporaneous labels.
review_questions.protocol_span: Dose-limiting toxicities observed during dose escalation included grade 3 increased alanine aminotransferase (240 mg daily) and grade 4 dyspnoea (300 mg daily).
review_questions.search_query: FDA ALK inhibitor prescribing information dosage modifications hepatotoxicity pulmonary toxicity pancreatic enzymes

review_questions.hypothesis: Eligibility may omit washout and recovery requirements after prior anticancer therapy, potentially confounding DLT attribution and early safety assessments.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Review actual eligibility criteria for washout periods, prior ALK/EGFR inhibitors, radiotherapy, residual toxicity, and justified exceptions. Use analogous trials only to contextualize design, not as binding standards.
review_questions.protocol_span: Eligible patients were at least 18 years of age and had advanced malignancies, including ALK-rearranged NSCLC, and disease that was refractory to available therapies or for which no curative treatments existed.
review_questions.search_query: ICH E8 clinical trial eligibility prior therapy washout residual toxicity dose limiting toxicity attribution oncology

review_questions.hypothesis: A standard 3 + 3 escalation alone may not estimate an optimal dose or characterize toxicity sufficiently to justify the initially selected RP2D.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Obtain dose-level allocations, DLT window and definitions, evaluable counts, escalation decisions, target toxicity criterion, and simulations or operating-characteristic analyses; account for the trial's historical date.
review_questions.protocol_span: In the initial dose-escalation phase 1 stage of the trial, patients received oral DV-R02 at total daily doses of 30-300 mg (according to a standard 3 + 3 design).
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dose optimization guidance 3+3 design maximum tolerated dose recommended phase 2 dose operating characteristics

review_questions.hypothesis: The five expansion cohorts may lack prespecified sample-size rationales and stopping rules despite substantially different populations and response estimands.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Retrieve the cohort-specific statistical plan: objectives, planned enrollment, response benchmarks, precision or error criteria, interim decisions, and safety/futility stopping rules. Determine which FDA guidance was applicable when cohorts opened.
review_questions.protocol_span: We enrolled patients in phase 2 into five cohorts: ALK inhibitor-naive ALK-rearranged NSCLC (cohort 1), crizotinib-treated ALK-rearranged NSCLC (cohort 2), DV-R02-positive NSCLC and resistance to one previous EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (cohort 3), other cancers with abnormalities in DV-R02 targets (cohort 4), and crizotinib-naive or crizotinib-treated ALK-rearranged NSCLC with active, measurable, intracranial CNS metastases (cohort 5).

review_questions.what_to_verify: Find scheduled intensive and trough sampling, day-1 and steady-state time points, analytes, adherence records, and coverage of each regimen; test whether sampling supports accumulation and exposure–response analyses.
review_questions.protocol_span: In the phase 2 expansion stage, we assessed three oral once-daily regimens: 90 mg, 180 mg, and 180 mg with a 7 day lead-in at 90 mg; one patient received 90 mg twice daily.
